cards.title: Show HN: Drop – a rootless Linux sandbox with gVisor support

signals.title: Show HN: Drop – a rootless Linux sandbox with gVisor support
signals.description:
I created Drop because I always felt uneasy installing and running third-party programs using my main user account. A single compromised dependency means a full compromise of the system. What is even worse, because I ship software from my computer, a single compromised dependency can lead to compromise of all the users of my software.

Containers and VMs are one solution, but for local work, they are often detrimental to productivity. It takes effort to configure a machine with all the tools and configs needed for productive work, but a container or a VM will be stripped of all these tools. This is great for production deployments, where the aim is a reproducible system with minimal dependencies, but can get in the way of productive local work.

Drop is language independent, but the workflow is inspired by Python's virtualenv. With virtualenv the environment isolation is only a convention that relies on installed dependencies being good citizens. With Drop the isolation is enforced.

Each Drop environment gets its own writable and easily disposable home dir, with only selected config files and dirs from the original home mounted, mostly read-only.

Drop uses Linux namespaces for isolation (user, mount, network, PID, IPC, cgroup), doesn't require root and, as an option, uses gVisor user-space kernel, which adds protection against exploiting host kernel vulnerabilities to escape the sandbox.

I don't want to make the introductory post too lengthy, but I'm here to answer any questions and give any additional technical details.

Note: This is my 3rd submission of the project, the first two did not draw attention. Since then I have added support for gVisor and created a project website to better explain the concept and organize documentation.

cards.title: Show HN: Hack – my Hacker News mobile client now lets you block AI posts

signals.title: Show HN: Hack – my Hacker News mobile client now lets you block AI posts
signals.description:
Hello HN!

I am the developer for HACK, a hacker news client that I have been building and maintaining for over 8 years now on iOS, iPadOS, MacOS and Android.

Wanted to share this news as there's been a ton of interest in these features recently.

Now, you can block AI related posts in the app. You can also disable infinite scrolling to prevent you from doomscrolling.

To enable these, go to app's home screen, then go to settings (top right), then scroll all the way to the bottom and enable these settings.

You can see an example of the effectiveness of the AI blocking toggle below. Across 3 pages of the HN front page which would typically load 90 posts (30 posts per page), a total of 32 post titles were blocked:

https://imgur.com/a/QtcHArF

Full list of all titles which were blocked can be seen here:

https://pastebin.com/HWnv3KrF

You can see this list of blocked posts by tapping the menu button, then "See Blocked Posts".

Currently, these features are available on Apple platforms. I am adding them to the Android client at this moment too.

You can try the Apple versions here:

https://apps.apple.com/ca/app/hack-for-hacker-news-yc-reader...

Feel free to ask questions.

cards.title: Show HN: CircuitPilot – We built a physics engine to auto-route PCBs using LLMs

signals.title: Show HN: CircuitPilot – We built a physics engine to auto-route PCBs using LLMs
signals.description:
Hey HN,

We wanted to see if we could build an AI agent that actually designs real, manufacturable PCBs from natural language, rather than just spitting out text.

LLMs are great at logic but terrible at spatial reasoning. So we decoupled them: we use an LLM (OpenAI/Claude/Local) to extract a component manifest and run an IPC-rules check (the "Critic"), and then we pass that to a custom Native Python Engine we wrote from scratch.

The Python engine uses a Force-Directed Graph simulation. Components repel each other, but electrical nets act as Hooke's Law springs, pulling related components together. Then it routes the traces using a net-aware shortest-path algorithm with 45-degree chamfers and multi-layer vias.

The result is a .kicad_pcb file that you can download directly from our React UI (rendered with KiCanvas) and open in KiCad.

We've made it totally open source. You can run it locally with a single docker-compose up command.

Repo: https://github.com/Paramveersingh-S/CircuitPilot We'd love your feedback on the routing engine!

cards.title: Show HN: Numban reports scammers callback number rather than spoofed caller ID

signals.title: Show HN: Numban reports scammers callback number rather than spoofed caller ID
signals.description:
I get a LOT of scam calls every week and cannot reliably block them because they spoof their caller ID. But they CANNOT spoof the call back number they leave on my voicemail.

So I made Numban - You share the voicemail left by scammers, Numban extracts the call back number they left, looks up the carrier or RespOrg, and files an abuse complaint.

Numban checks the number periodically and when it detects that it has been disconnected, it lets you know that you helped kill a number. There's a leaderboard to track reports and kills.

The goal is not just to file abuse reports but to also establish a pattern of organizations that enable these scumbags.

So help out! Install the app (iPhone only for now) and tap "share" next to a scam voicemail. It will transcribe it and ask you to verify the correct number and then we'll file the abuse reports.

Hopefully with enough data we can shut down some of these operations by cutting off the phone number suppliers.

Testing is helpful and if anyone knows a lot about TCPA, phone routing, RespOrgs, and associated legal recourse, I would love to talk to you!

cards.title: Show HN: Kado – Search to Allow Personal Agents to Find Agent Apps

signals.title: Show HN: Kado – Search to Allow Personal Agents to Find Agent Apps
signals.description:
Hey folks!

My cofounder and I have built Kado - Search for Personal Agents to find Agent Apps[1].

We think the future of agents that individuals will use few personal agents (think, personal computers) as their primary interface, and while those agents delegate work to agent apps to complete actual tasks.

We were building a personal agent ourselves when we noticed that our users were often trying to do complex things which should be delegated away. We found that web search didn't cut it for reasons including the "quality metric" being incorrect, and a "don't know what to search for" problem.

Kado's crawl uses LLMs to parse information from websites pages, agent cards, or other discovery sources to model the actual outcome(s) that's being promised, and the interface to them (we call these "agent apps").

Our search and index is based on a heavily modified version of HyDE. The search itself is quite slow right now because of LLMs in the loop. We want to get this down to ~sub-second.

We have ~3000 indexed MCPs and/or A2A agents, and we recently purged the index of entries your agents can't use (we had ~45k before that). I'm partial to a TTRPG character generator MCP that's great for printed one shot sheets, but some others you may also want to try searching for include builder/research/crawl tools or (surprisingly) financial data tools. Also, did you know that AWS has a public devops/root cause analysis agent?[2]

The best way to try it is to install it on your agent (it's a CLI + Skill for now, MCP coming soon!) but you can also just try direct searches on the website. The website requires a google login for spam protection (which we want to remove if we get some funding haha), but the CLI does not need a login (we use proof of work to prevent spam, and an agent identity based on a keypair is auto-created and stored in your keychain).

Would love any feedback!

cards.title: Show HN: Brig – A MicroVM sandbox for AI coding agents on Mac and Linux

signals.title: Show HN: Brig – A MicroVM sandbox for AI coding agents on Mac and Linux
signals.description:
Hi HN, I’m Spiros from NOFire AI. We’ve open-sourced Brig under Apache 2.0.

Brig runs AI coding agents inside a microVM on Mac (Apple Silicon) and Linux (x86_64/ARM). It came out of our work on controlled autonomy for production remediation. The same isolation is useful when running coding agents with auto-approval on your own machine.

The agent gets its own Linux kernel. You choose the project and credentials to share. The shared project remains writable, and the default network allows internet access.

After installation, brig run claude starts Claude Code inside the sandbox.

All components are Apache 2.0, including the microVMM, which is under 20,000 lines of code. The README covers installation, the architecture and the security model.

cards.title: Show HN: Warble – Share voice notes in your social media feeds

signals.title: Show HN: Warble – Share voice notes in your social media feeds
signals.description:
Hey HN,

I built Warble because I noticed that you can't currently share voice notes to your main social feeds.

With Warble you can simply record a voice note, choose a theme, and warble quickly renders out a video you can share. No editing required, no need to get on camera.

The output isn't genAI video, the videos themselves are pre-designed motion templates (I'm primarily a motion designer). AI is used in a small way to transcribe the voice note and provide the captions which are then animated within each of the themes.

I've been using it myself to post over on LinkedIn for a month or so now and it's helped me post consistently, something I've never really stuck to. The act of simply recording a voice note makes the whole process much easier.

There's a free trial to get a feel for it if you fancy checking it out.

cards.title: Show HN: An API that tells you what people love about a product

signals.title: Show HN: An API that tells you what people love about a product
signals.description:
YC says "make something people want." But how would you know if you made something that people want? We made something to help you find exactly that.

The thing is, they're already telling you what they love in reviews, comments, and online forums. The hard part is pulling it all together.

So we built an API that does that. Give it a brand + product name (only consumer goods work for now). It searches for thousands of reviews per product across Amazon, TikTok, Reddit, YouTube, Instagram, Walmart, and other web sources. Then, it extracts positive sentiments that consistently repeat across reviews and shows you the evidence (actual quotes + links to the reviews). These are the features people love about your product.

It takes a few minutes per product. Costs $0.99 each. Creating a key gives you $1 of credit, so the first product analysis is free.

Docs: https://bb-product-api-docs.web.app/ Get API key: https://bb-product-api-docs.web.app/keys.html Examples: https://bb-product-api-docs.web.app/examples.html

Please let me know if we can add anything to make it more useful. Ask me anything.
